dialogue.gensokyou.rinnosuke.greet:
Ah, a customer. I am Rinnosuke Morichika, keeper of the Kourindou.
Though my shop sits at the edge of Gensokyo, most of my wares are oddities scavenged from the outside world.
Youkai, humans, gods... I have long since stopped being surprised by anyone.
If you have some object you cannot make sense of, bring it to me -- for the right price, I can tell you its origin.
Of course, if it is the kind of object that invites trouble, that is an entirely different matter.
dialogue.gensokyou.rinnosuke.wares:
Curious about my stock?
Yen, gold coins, fragments of spell cards... anything rare enough from the outside world, and I likely have one or two hidden away.
But a warning: prices are fixed, no haggling, and if you break something you pay full price.
The barrier has been unstable lately, and outside objects grow scarcer by the day -- buy while you can.

gensokyou.book.entry.fantasy_materials_o: Every specialty material in Gensokyo comes from one of five resource rituals: ores from the mountain god, earth from Haniyasu, wood from Kukunochi, the sea from Watatsumi, plants from Kaya no Hime.$(br2)Sacrifice the matching tool on a ritual pedestal and the ritual will hand you that line of produce in batches. The material never matters: a wooden pickaxe and a netherite axe are one and the same to a god.

Produce comes in bands. Place a guidebook on the pedestal to draw from the low band; a sukima fragment opens the high band along with it.$(br)Offer three wither skeleton skulls for nether goods, or a dragon head for end goods. These are tokens only, and the ritual never eats them.

The most important of these are the three minerals: cinnabar, spirit iron and star silver. They arrive as raw ore and must be melted in Kanayamahiko's Forge, with spirit charcoal as the reagent in a fixed ratio, before they become pure material.$(br)Cinnabar and spirit iron take one charcoal each; star silver takes two.
gensokyou.book.entry.item_recipe.craftin: This starter core can be built at a workbench, with no ritual to power it yet. While you have no other source of spirit, it is what gets your first ritual circle running.
gensokyou.book.entry.item_recipe.p1: The Circle of Creation fuses the offerings on its pedestals into this item. Bring the right offerings to a ritual circle of the matching tier, and have enough spirit stored.
gensokyou.book.entry.item_recipe.pedesta: Pedestals hold the offerings a ritual needs. They can be built at a workbench, costing no spirit and requiring no ritual to exist yet; once the core stands and the pattern is laid, place one offering on each pedestal to begin.
gensokyou.book.entry.material_earth.p1: Haniyasu makes vessels of clay, and everything the ground yields - dirt, clay, even the soil of the far shore - is hers to give for a shovel.
gensokyou.book.entry.material_marine.p1: The palace of Watatsumi holds sanzu flasks, spirit fish and mermaid scales; tide crystals and dragon scales lie deeper still. Offer a fishing rod and the sea opens its vaults.
gensokyou.book.entry.material_ores.p1: The hardest things in the rock. Offer a pickaxe to Oyamatsumi and he will trade ore blocks of cinnabar and spirit iron.$(br2)Both are still raw: send them to Kanayamahiko's Forge with one spirit charcoal each. Star silver lies deeper and takes two.
gensokyou.book.entry.material_plants.p1: Kaya no Hime tends every grass and flower in Gensokyo. Offer a hoe and she will bloom new ones in her garden.
gensokyou.book.entry.material_refined_ci: Cinnabar is the source of Gensokyo's vermilion. Ore from the mountain goes into Kanayamahiko's Forge with one spirit charcoal and comes out at its purest.$(br2)Too little charcoal and the fire never catches - the forge waits until the ratio is met.
gensokyou.book.entry.material_spirit_cha: Spirit charcoal is what Kanayamahiko's Forge burns. Without it the fire never catches, and no ore will melt.$(br2)Smother sacred wood into spirit charcoal at the Circle of Creation: four charcoal, four sacred wood, a thousand spirit.

Cinnabar and spirit iron each take one charcoal; star silver takes two. Short of charcoal, the forge does not go out - it holds the job and waits for you to top it up, and only then begins.$(br)Outside the forge, spirit charcoal serves nothing else.
gensokyou.book.entry.material_spirit_iro: Heavier than cinnabar, and every ritual and tool knows it well. Spirit iron ore plus one spirit charcoal in the forge yields refined spirit iron.
gensokyou.book.entry.material_star_silve: Star silver lies deepest in the mountain and only answers to a sukima fragment; it is also the hardest to melt - both star silver ore and rough star silver ore take two charcoal.$(br2)Refined star silver is the frame of danmaku weapons and advanced cores.
gensokyou.book.entry.material_wood.p1: Sacred wood and magic wood come from Kukunochi's grove; eternal wood needs one more token of trust. Offer an axe and take the timber.
gensokyou.book.entry.item_landscaping_to: A spirit-fed demolition tool for laying out large ritual sites. Place it on the ground and right-click to open its panel; set the length (X) and width (Z) centered on the device, and the height (Y) rising from the block below it.$(br2)It clears the box to bare ground and paves the bottom layer with dirt.

It deletes everything inside the box - terrain, trees, even chests - except ritual structure blocks and bedrock, and the dirt floor never replaces bedrock.$(br2)Each activation costs spirit equal to base x length x width x height: a full 32x32x24 box runs about 100,000, after which the device goes on cooldown. Creative mode pays nothing.
gensokyou.book.entry.item_spirit_bomb.p1: A placeable, reusable detonator. Place it, then right-click to set the fuse (0.1-600 s), power (1-12) and blast radius (1-24).$(br2)Press Arm to begin the countdown; the cost is drawn from your own spirit pool and the bomb refuses to arm when you are short.
gensokyou.book.entry.item_spirit_bomb.p2: Cost is base x (power/4)^2 x (radius/6) - a full power 12, radius 24 charge runs about 20,000.$(br2)The blast drops every block it destroys, and the detonator itself falls back as an item afterwards, ready to be used again. The countdown keeps running even while you are away.
gensokyou.book.entry.monsters_fairies.p1: Fairy grunts hover above you and rain danmaku; defeating one always drops a Memory Fragment.
gensokyou.book.entry.monsters_fairies.p2: Great fairies are tougher mini-bosses firing three-shot fans; defeating one yields this very book.
gensokyou.book.entry.npcs_overview.p1: Beyond the youkai, some residents will talk with you, offering information, trade and requests.
gensokyou.book.entry.npcs_overview.p2: Talking to NPCs advances the story and unlocks new book pages.
gensokyou.book.entry.preface.p1: Welcome, outsider chosen by Gensokyo. This book unfolds with your journey: unseen content is never spoiled early. Only when you truly reach the Nether and the End will those pages surface.
gensokyou.book.entry.preface.p2: Should you ever lose this book, take heart: the Memory Fragments scattered across Gensokyo can be gathered, nine of them to piece a new one together.
gensokyou.book.entry.ritual.hyakki_yagyo: Beneath the torii, four stone lanterns light in turn. Those who keep the shrine say that after dusk, if no one offers incense, the wandering spirits on the mountain path gather here -- not out of malice, but because they remember someone once waited for them.$(br2)That is the Night Parade of a Hundred Demons.

Lay out the offerings and press Summon. The rite takes no admission fee, but the core will still call for enough spirit from its surroundings, turning your offerings into a black-red sphere heavy enough to tear a seam.$(br2)While the supply runs short it simply hangs there -- it does not hurry, and it does not die. The moment it fills, the sphere bursts and a golden column climbs from the altar to the sky. As for the offerings, they were gone the moment you pressed the button.
The Circle of Creation fuses offerings into something new. Star Shift undoes that: it takes a single amplify core apart and writes it again from nothing.$(br2)Take the core off its weapon first — it cannot be washed where it lies — and set it in the Amp Core slot of the ritual core. Zhao Hua's four offerings go on the pedestals as always, and the dial begins to turn.$(br2)How far it can reach depends on how high you built. A first-tier circle only reaches tier 1 cores: one affix, thirty thousand spirit. A third tier reaches tier 2 as well, three affixes for three million. A fifth reaches tier 3, five affixes for three hundred million. The price follows the core, never the circle.

When the dial settles, it lays the new core beside the old one, affix by affix. Take the whole new writing, or keep what you had. There is no half-measure — you cannot keep one affix and take another — and keeping refunds nothing. The spirit is spent either way; only stopping during the gathering gives it back.$(br2)Only the one who began the wash may decide. Others may open the core and read the result, but the choice is not theirs to make.$(br2)An unfinished wash waits indefinitely. Close the interface, log out, come back — the dial is still where you left it, and nothing spoils while you are away. Have your spirit ready before you start. At the higher tiers a single turn costs more than most circles hold at once, and the dial is not interested in what the core was worth to you before.
gensokyou.book.entry.rituals_basics.p1: A ritual centres on a Ritual Core; build the circle from ritual stones, then place offerings on the pedestals to start it.
gensokyou.book.entry.rituals_basics.p2: Use the builder to preview the pattern; higher-tier ritual stones raise the tier a ritual can reach.
gensokyou.book.entry.spellcards_overview: Spell cards are manifested danmaku moves you can cast once equipped.

Spell Card Stars are among the rarest materials: the broken shards never appear on their own and are only taken from fallen enemies, and eight shards reforge into one whole star in the Circle of Creation. Gathering them means facing something dangerous first.
gensokyou.book.entry.healing_garden.p1: The Sea of Flowers once spilled across the fairy's garden, and rain-springs shimmered between the petals. She still believes that wherever blossoms bloom, even the deepest wounds are tended in time.
gensokyou.book.entry.healing_garden.p2: Raise a garden whose blossoms never fade. Those who stand within are wrapped in gentle life and healed moment by moment. The garden grants no spirit, and it will not mend those who mean it harm.
gensokyou.book.entry.flower_armor.p1: The great fairy was never one for battle. All she can do is weave the softest petals, one by one, into a mantle and set it between herself and harm.
gensokyou.book.entry.flower_armor.p2: A mantle of petals circles you. When danmaku strikes it, the blow is negated and a petal falls away; against close blades and falling impacts, the petals can do nothing.
gensokyou.book.entry.demarcation.p1: Rumia hates to be seen. A single gesture and the light is shut outside - in the dark there is no direction, and no prey. Yet should you lash out, the darkness learns where you are first.
gensokyou.book.entry.demarcation.p2: Spread a field of darkness around yourself. Foes within lose your shape and their bearings, and even the fiercest youkai hesitate in place. The moment you wound anything yourself, the darkness scatters.
gensokyou.book.entry.spider_web.p1: Deep in the valley the webs never see light, yet they always wait for a passerby. Kurodani Yamame weaves her threads into an unseen prison - struggle only draws it tighter.
gensokyou.book.entry.spider_web.p2: Spit a silken thread ahead of your crosshair; where it lands, a web unfurls to blanket the area. Everything caught in it - even legendary youkai - finds every step a struggle. Only the weaver is left unbound.
gensokyou.book.entry.plague_repay.p1: They say Kurodani Yamame can carry another's illness away. She gathers the plague into herself, then returns it, unchanged, to whoever brought the calamity.
gensokyou.book.entry.plague_repay.p2: For a while, no new affliction can take hold of you; and anything that dares wound you is repaid with plague, taking on several maladies at once. Old ailments already upon you are not washed away.
gensokyou.book.entry.fox_servant.p1: Yukari's shikigami is famed for its flawless schemes. This lone fox-fire is but a 'sham', yet it too knows how to choose its prey - it pounces, nests in the victim, and stays until the shell burns to cinders before seeking the next.
gensokyou.book.entry.fox_servant.p2: Summon a fox-fire to trail you. It darts at the nearest foe in range and possesses it on impact, leaving that body forever burning and steadily wounded; when it is spent or you have drifted away, the fox-fire rises again to hunt the next target.
gensokyou.book.entry.term_basics.p1: Spirit: the energy that casts and sustains rituals. It regenerates over time and can be stored in crystals and rituals.
gensokyou.book.entry.term_basics.p2: Superhuman tier: your level of mastery over spirit; many rituals and refinements gate on it.
gensokyou.book.entry.weapons_overview.p1: Danmaku weapons fire elemental danmaku; melee weapons reward timing and feel.
gensokyou.book.entry.weapons_overview.p2: Upgrade slots and rune affixes further shape how a weapon performs.
gensokyou.book.landing: Welcome to Gensokyo. This book collects the basics of spirit, spell cards, rituals, creatures, NPCs and weapons.
